items.title: "한국 책 수십만권 사들여 AI 학습?"…최휘영 "현행법으론 대응 한계"
items.excerpt: 미국 AI 기업 앤트로픽의 한국 도서 대량 구매·무단 학습 논란에 대해 최휘영 문화체육관광부 장관이 현행법으로는 대응에 한계가 있다고 밝혔다.

items.title: 판권에 ‘AI 학습 거부’ 못 박고, 사용료도 받고···유럽 출판계의 반격
items.excerpt: 독일 미디어 플랫폼 DPR 창립자 슈테펜 마이어는 유럽 출판사들이 판권면 AI 학습 거부 조항, AI 기업과의 개별 라이선스 계약, 업계 공동 대응 등 세 갈래로 움직이고 있다고 소개했다.

items.title: 에이아이 학습용 출판물, 정당한 거래 시장 열려야 [.txt]
items.excerpt: 백원근의 출판 풍향계: 프랑크푸르트 도서전의 '프랑크푸르트 호소문' 등 국내외 출판계가 AI 학습에 쓰인 저작물에 대한 정당한 거래 시장을 요구하고 있다.

items.title: 에듀클라우드닷컴·KL매니지먼트, AI 음악으로 K문학 해외 홍보
items.excerpt: 출판 저작권 에이전시 KL매니지먼트와 에듀클라우드닷컴이 해외 판권 계약이 이뤄진 한국 소설의 인물·장면·메시지를 AI 음악 테마곡으로 만들어 글로벌 독자 홍보에 쓰기로 했다.

items.title: Google takes Dreambeans to India in bid to bring AI-generated personal stories to the masses
items.excerpt: Google's Dreambeans, which generates illustrated personalized stories from users' Gmail, Photos and YouTube activity without a prompt (some animated via Veo), now supports 13 Indian languages in its first market outside the U.S.

items.title: The Gruffalo's illustrator is threatening legal action against AI companies — so I put ChatGPT and Gemini's copyright safeguards to the test
items.excerpt: Axel Scheffler says his Gruffalo images are being pumped out of AI models and is weighing legal action; TechRadar tested whether ChatGPT and Gemini would recreate the picture-book characters.

items.title: AI’s role in book publishing raises questions about quality, transparency
items.excerpt: AI is changing how authors write, edit and publish books, but its growing use has some readers questioning the quality of what they're buying and whether authors should disclose AI use.

items.title: "I steamed up my Kindle." The founder of DOU and Djinni created his own AI-powered e-reader with the help of Claude — it even works with paper books
items.excerpt: Max Ishchenko, founder of DOU and Djinni, built his own reading service with built-in AI explanations and translations using Claude, after being disappointed by standard e-reader features.

items.title: From AI Adoption to AI Practice: Building Governed AI in Scholarly Publishing
items.excerpt: How a publisher can make AI useful across the organization while keeping control of confidential information, editorial decisions and accountability.

items.title: Guest Post — What AI Can’t Learn About Peer Review… Because Nobody Can Explain It
items.excerpt: What might be lost if publishers automate peer review with AI without first understanding the tacit expertise behind it.

items.title: Cleveland Public Library sets rules for how it will use AI
items.excerpt: The Cleveland Public Library board approved an AI governance policy that creates a staff AI council and sets rules for how the library will use AI tools.

items.title: Why the AI Detection Scandals Will End—Probably Quite Soon
items.excerpt: Jane Friedman argues 2026's AI-use allegations against authors stem from books acquired before publishers adopted detection tools like Pangram, so the scandals may soon fade.

items.title: Copyright Infringement Lawsuit Against OpenAI Draws More than 50 (Very Illuminating) Amicus Briefs
items.excerpt: More than 50 amicus briefs filed in the authors' copyright case against OpenAI map the arguments over fair use and AI training on books. (Follow-up to publishers' amicus brief covered 10-30.)

items.title: 한국출판인회의, AI 시대 출판 논의하는 ‘2026 아시아 출판 주간’ 개최
items.excerpt: 한국출판인회의가 아시아 각 지역 출판인을 초청해 AI 시대 출판이 나아갈 방향을 모색하는 '2026 아시아 출판 주간'을 연다.

items.title: News Podcast: Audible Lets Listeners Talk to Dracula; Plaintiffs Drop a Key AI Study Against OpenAI
items.excerpt: ALLi's Dan Holloway on Audible's generative-AI feature that lets listeners converse with Dracula, an OpenAI case twist, and Books by People.
